claims.text: Adding approximately 0.5–1.0 at.% B to a CoFeCrNi-based magnetic high-entropy alloy will create B-rich solute clusters or boride precipitates.
The B-rich clusters or boride precipitates will impede domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion will increase coercive field relative to an undoped baseline.
The initial CoFeCrNi-based magnetic high-entropy alloy is single phase after arc melting and homogenization.
Annealing after B addition will promote uniform boride precipitation or B-rich cluster formation.
The predicted effect should hold after inert-atmosphere melting and casting, homogenization near 1000 °C for about 24 hours, and air cooling.
B-rich zones or boride precipitates will occur both at grain boundaries and within grains.
B additions stabilize domain-wall pinning centers.
The coercive-field increase will be on the order of tens of percent.
The relevant comparison is an otherwise identical CoFeCrNi-based alloy without B, processed in the same manner.
B concentrations above approximately 1.0 at.% may produce unwanted phases.
B concentrations above approximately 1.0 at.% may cause embrittlement.
Unwanted phases or embrittlement above approximately 1.0 at.% B may offset coercivity benefits.
Compositional modification of a magnetic high-entropy alloy can alter coercivity.
Magnetic-alloy doping alters coercivity through enhanced domain-wall pinning.
A lack of statistically significant coercivity increase in the B-doped samples under the specified matched conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the predicted B-rich clusters or boride precipitates would falsify the proposed structural-mediator pathway.
